BLOCKER: Unreadable/corrupt `config/residency-policy.json` silently defaults `gate_mode` to warn (`_policy()` returns `{}` → `"warn"`), and a malformed `gate_mode_expires` keeps warn — a compliance gate must fail closed; this contradicts the shipped doc ("unreadable policy always blocks").

Go `Validate` has no missing-group check for `egress` (only 5 of 6 groups), so an empty/missing egress group passes the Go authority while Python fails it → parity mismatch → gate exit 2, an "execution failure" warn mode cannot downgrade. Violates AC2 and the warn-never-downgrades-failures rule.

AC5's required single conformance fixture set (valid + every RESIDENCY_* code incl. schema/invalid-field/toolchain/profile, yielding identical pass/block from `core.packaging.validate` and `cmd/pfresidency`) is absent; the existing Python/Go divergences are therefore untested and unverified.
MAJOR: Go CLI never emits `RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME`/`RESIDENCY_PROFILE_UNREADABLE` as report codes — it exits 2 pre-validation, so the gate maps unknown home to `RESIDENCY_VALIDATOR_UNAVAILABLE` (exit 2). The gate's `hard` set references codes the Go path can never return; unknown home is a policy violation, not a tool failure.

`--report` returns exit 0 even on execution failures (`return 0 if a.report else 2`), masking validator-unavailable/toolchain breakage — violates "warn/report downgrades policy violations only, never execution failures".

Dual validators already diverge: Python strips `utf-8-sig`, Go `json.Unmarshal` fails on a BOM (this repo demonstrably has BOM'd configs) → gate exit 2; parity compares only booleans, so code-set drift is invisible. This duplication is a long-term maintenance hazard.
Override precedence (`products/<project>/residency-manifest.json`) is untested; no test exercises `residency_path` override or a per-project build with an override present.
Python appends unstable text into a frozen-code contract (`RESIDENCY_MANIFEST_UNREADABLE:<exception>`, raw exception strings) — codes leak paths and break the versioned error-code contract.
MINOR: JSONL rotation moves `.jsonl.2`→`.3` then unconditionally deletes `.3`, so only 2 rotated files survive; the "5MB x3" registry claim and the loop body are wrong.
First exception path writes the event but never prints the report even with `--report`, unlike the second path — inconsistent observability.
`_report` dumps full JSON to stdout on any failure even without `--report`, noisying normal CI logs.
The event record lacks expiry/downgrade metadata (no record that warn was escalated by `gate_mode_expires`), weakening auditability.

`config/residency-policy.json` ownership assigned to `go/backupdrill/region.go` (a source file) is a weak ownership model for a compliance lever; `residency-gate.json` declares 90-day rotated retention but is never rotated.
Gate invokes `go run` (compile) on every fast-tier run; a prebuilt binary is cheaper for a fast gate.
NIT: `id-blocks.json` session-reservation bump rides along unrelated to BI-PF-1304.
Empty home in Python loads `-v1.json` and adds `RESIDENCY_PROFILE_UNREADABLE` noise beside `RESIDENCY_UNKNOWN_HOME`.
SUMMARY: Shape is right (template + override, profile bounds, Go authority, bounded events, warn-first), but the gate fails open on unreadable policy and on `--report` masking execution failures.

The Go and Python validators already diverge on egress group, BOM, and unknown-home semantics, and the required single conformance fixture set proving pass/block parity is missing — parity today is unverifiable.
Ship only after: fail-closed policy read, egress missing-group in Go, unknown-home emitted as a code (not exit 2), and one shared fixture set driving both validators.
